extracted.intended_audience: educators, curriculum designers, teachers, and students of educational theory
extracted.subtask_description: Principles for organizing school curricula and pedagogy that integrate science, direct experience, imagination, and the fine arts to cultivate genuine appreciation, social progress, and intellectual emancipation. Focuses on what makes subject-matter educative and how to value studies in schooling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful understanding over rote knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: "Knowing" the definitions, rules, formulae, etc., is like knowing the names of parts of a machine without knowing what they do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach elements of subject-matter in relation to the problems in which they function and their specific utility. Avoid instruction that makes information an end in itself or reduces knowledge to mere names; emphasize what each element accomplishes in the system of which it is a member.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational use of science to modify imagination and feeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Education must use science in a way to modify the habitual attitude of imagination and feeling, not leave it just an extension of our physical arms and legs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not confine science instruction to technical skill or means; aim to reshape ends and desires by exposing learners to scientific perspectives that broaden imaginative and emotional outlooks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach scientific method to emancipate from rule-of-thumb
rubrics_metrics.description: The method of science engrained through education in habit means emancipation from rule of thumb and from the routine generated by rule of thumb procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instill experimental habits—using past experiences as tools rather than masters—so reason operates within experience. Avoid accepting empirical as merely crude or unrational practice; foster deliberate testing, inference, and systematic inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science as agent of social progress and formation of new ends
rubrics_metrics.description: Science marks the emancipation of mind from devotion to customary purposes and makes possible the systematic pursuit of new ends; it enriches prior purposes and forms new ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame science education to show how scientific discovery opens possibilities, changes desires, and leads to social and technical innovations. Emphasize development of goals, not only improved means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid treating applied knowledge as inferior to 'pure' theory
rubrics_metrics.description: The notion that 'applied' knowledge is somehow less worthy than 'pure' knowledge is a survival of an aristocratic culture and cripples educational use of both studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value useful or industrial arts alongside theoretical study; incorporate practical, occupationally-relevant problems to prevent elitist narrowing of curriculum and to make knowledge genuinely humanistic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach abstraction, generalization, and formulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstraction deliberately selects from former experiences that which is thought helpful in dealing with the new; generalization is the counterpart of abstraction; formulation is essential to the completion of the work of thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Help students detach common features from particulars and give them names and propositions (formulations) so that individual experience is rendered transferable and usable by others. Emphasize that formulation is not an afterthought but crucial to thinking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use laboratory and practical work to supply first-hand background
rubrics_metrics.description: The laboratory may be treated as an additional resource to supply conditions and appliances for the better pursuit of these problems... in a high school or college the first and basic function of laboratory work is to familiarize the student at first hand with a certain range of facts and problems—to give him a 'feeling' for them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize hands-on and problem-centered activities that give students direct acquaintance with phenomena before abstract instruction. Labs and active occupations serve as preparatory experience for symbolic learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide direct (realizing) experiences before symbolic instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Before teaching can safely enter upon conveying facts and ideas through the media of signs, schooling must provide genuine situations in which personal participation brings home the import of the material and the problems which it conveys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure students have qualitatively appropriate direct experiences (play, active occupations, laboratory work) that connect with later symbolic/formal instruction; without this background, symbolic instruction risks being 'bookish' and remote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage imagination in all fields to secure appreciation
rubrics_metrics.description: Only a personal response involving imagination can possibly procure realization even of pure 'facts'... The engagement of the imagination is the only thing that makes any activity more than mechanical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize play and manual/laboratory activities as imaginative enterprises and exploit imagination across subjects to prevent reduction of serious work to rote technique. Avoid confining imagination to 'fine art' or childish play.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fine arts and literature as chief agencies of intensified appreciation
rubrics_metrics.description: As engaging the emotions and the imagination, [arts] have the qualities which give the fine arts their quality... they are the chief agencies of an intensified, enhanced appreciation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include literature, music, drawing, painting, etc., not as luxuries but as central to fixing taste, forming standards of worth, and arousing a demand for better conditions; use arts to reveal depth in ordinary experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form values through lived, appreciable experience, not only symbolic teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Working as distinct from professed standards depend upon what an individual has himself specifically appreciated to be deeply significant in concrete situations... Without this vital appreciation, the duty and virtue impressed upon him by others as a standard remains purely a matter of symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design learning experiences that allow pupils to internalize values (honesty, kindness, clarity) through practice and personal realization rather than merely teaching rules, marks, or verbal standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid external discipline as substitute for appreciable habits
rubrics_metrics.description: The premium so often put in schools upon external 'discipline,' and upon marks and rewards, upon promotion and keeping back, are the obverse of the lack of attention given to life situations in which the meaning of facts, ideas, principles, and problems is vitally brought home.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace reliance on punishment/reward systems with opportunities for meaningful participation that form tastes and working standards; prioritize situational, interest-based activities over mechanical discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not establish a rigid hierarchy of values among studies
rubrics_metrics.description: We cannot establish a hierarchy of values among studies... In so far as any study has a unique or irreplaceable function in experience, its worth is intrinsic or incomparable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist attempts to rank subjects absolutely (one above another); recognize both intrinsic (appreciative) and instrumental (comparative) values and evaluate studies relative to contexts and ends rather than by blanket hierarchies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalization as a social device enabling wide perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Generalization is essentially a social device... Scientific abstraction and generalization are equivalent to taking the point of view of any man, whatever his location in time and space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach generalization to broaden viewpoint beyond local customs and narrow groups; emphasize social applicability and transferability of abstractions so pupils can apply ideas to varied situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulation and naming to make abstractions shareable
rubrics_metrics.description: Names give abstract meanings a physical locus and body. Formulation is thus not an after-thought or by-product; it is essential to the completion of the work of thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide learners with vocabulary and propositional forms to fix and communicate abstractions; without formulation, valuable features of experience may perish with the individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use science education to foster belief in direction and improvement of human affairs
rubrics_metrics.description: The problem of an educational use of science is then to create an intelligence pregnant with belief in the possibility of the direction of human affairs by itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orient science instruction toward instilling confidence that intelligence and systematic inquiry can address social evils (disease, poverty) and produce practical progress; use examples of scientific advances to illustrate constructive agency.
